name: NJ-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 5 points with a favorable national environment for Democrats
Mejia holds a large fundraising edge ($1.8M vs $658K) and faces no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds around 95%
No public general-election polling in the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to the incumbent: a Democratic-leaning district, a strong Democratic environment, incumbency, and a clear money advantage, with markets pricing a Democratic win near 95%. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals.
model.watch: Mejia's very low cash-on-hand relative to what she has raised could matter if Republican outside groups enter late.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Analilia Mejia defends a northern New Jersey seat that leans Democratic by about five points, in a year when the national environment favors her party. She has raised roughly $1.8 million to Republican Joe Hathaway's $658,000, and outside groups have spent only in her support, with no advertised opposition. Hathaway, however, has nearly exhausted his cash, holding just over $5,000, while Mejia also ends with a modest war chest of about $27,000.

Prediction markets give Mejia roughly a 95% chance of winning, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings are available to test that view. An independent candidate, Alan Bond, is on the ballot but shows no measurable fundraising or spending. All available evidence points to a comfortable Democratic hold.
